top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the criteria I stated in round 2 and in my profile: a voice audible in the writing and nowhere else, and sustained literary quality. On public knowledge, Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation into one imaginative structure, and the formal control over very long forms is part of the achievement. The citation scope is the prose architecture, with poetry named only as origin, since my knowledge of his poetry and shorter prose is thin. I cannot show from the texts that Solenoid changes the method rather than restating the trilogy, and I judge him through translation, not the Romanian sentence. If colleagues who read Romanian showed only restatement, I would narrow the citation. Adonis (P002) is a serious second. His renewal of a whole poetic language may be a broader achievement, but I cannot test the prosody or the later collections and the committee has no identified Arabic reader, so I cannot place him first. P000 is last because neither lead claim is so unstable that no defensible citation can be written. The open questions concern verification and wording, not whether the writers are distinctive.
